credit: Plates: public-domain images from Wikimedia Commons (the licence checked on each file page) and from the U.S. Geological Survey's photographic library (a federal work in the public domain), each named in its caption with the original. Resized for this site.

plates.caption: Photograph by the geologist T. Wayland Vaughan of the U.S. Geological Survey, 1908: arches of the Long Key viaduct standing in open water, the year the line reached Knight's Key. The viaduct had about 180 arches of fifty feet.
plates.source: U.S. Geological Survey Photographic Library, vtw00253, ScienceBase item 51ddc69be4b0f72b4472100b (https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/51ddc69be4b0f72b4472100b); U.S. public domain

plates.titel: Flagler's special on the Long Key viaduct
plates.caption: 'H.M. Flagler's Special, first train crossing Long Key Viaduct, 2.7 miles long.' Photograph by John N. Chamberlain, 1909 (Library of Congress). The line reached Knight's Key in February 1908; Key West only in 1912.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:H.M. Flagler's Special, first train crossing Long Key Viaduct, 2.7 miles long, Long Key, Fla. LCCN2005694817.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:H.M._Flagler%27s_Special,_first_train_crossing_Long_Key_Viaduct,_2.7_miles_long,_Long_Key,_Fla._LCCN2005694817.jpg)

plates.caption: From The New Student's Reference Work (1914): falsework and forms for one of the concrete arches. The engineering press counted some five hundred arches over about six miles.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:NSRW Florida Keys Railroad - building arch.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NSRW_Florida_Keys_Railroad_-_building_arch.jpg)

plates.caption: From The New Student's Reference Work (1914): a reinforced concrete pier in its cofferdam, the work that the storms of 1906 and 1909 swept away and that had to be begun again.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:NSRW Florida Keys Railroad - building pier.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NSRW_Florida_Keys_Railroad_-_building_pier.jpg)

plates.caption: 'Map of Florida Keys Showing Projected Extension of the Florida East Coast to Key West', The Railroad Gazette, 6 October 1905, p. 324: the line from Homestead across Key Largo and down the keys, 'completed line' and 'proposed line', six months after work began.
plates.source: The Railroad Gazette  1905-10-06: Vol 39 Iss 14 (1905-10-06), page image n15, archive.org sim_railway-age_1905-10-06_39_14 (https://archive.org/details/sim_railway-age_1905-10-06_39_14/page/n15); published in the United States before 1931, public domain

plates.caption: 'Floating camp or quarterboat': photograph from the railway's booklet for the opening, 1912. The men building the viaducts lived on such boats, moored behind the keys; in October 1906 a hurricane carried them out to sea.
plates.source: Key West extension, Florida East Coast Railway, opened January 22, 1912 (1912), page image n17, archive.org keywestextension00flor (https://archive.org/details/keywestextension00flor/page/n17); published in the United States before 1931, public domain

plates.titel: Arch center and spandrel wall forms, 1906
plates.caption: 'Arch Center and Spandrel Wall Forms Under Construction': the timber falsework for one of the concrete arches, with carpenters at work. From George P. Carver's article in The Engineering Record, 20 October 1906, p. 424.
plates.source: Engineering Record, Building Record and Sanitary Engineer  1906-10-20: Vol 54 Iss 16  (1906-10-20), page image n3, archive.org engineering-record_1906-10-20_54_16 (https://archive.org/details/engineering-record_1906-10-20_54_16/page/n3); published in the United States before 1931, public domain

plates.caption: 'Bahia Honda Bridge, Only Truss Bridge on Extension': the steel trusses over the deepest water of the line, where some piers stand 30 feet below tide. Railway Age Gazette, 10 May 1912, p. 1039.
plates.source: Railway Age Gazette  1912-05-10: Vol 52 Iss 19 (1912-05-10), page image n10, archive.org sim_railway-age_1912-05-10_52_19 (https://archive.org/details/sim_railway-age_1912-05-10_52_19/page/n10); published in the United States before 1931, public domain

plates.caption: 'Houseboat for Foremen': a two-storey houseboat moored at the shore, from Harry C. Smith's report in The Railroad Gazette, 20 April 1906, p. 405. Six months later the hurricane of October 1906 tore such boats from their moorings.
plates.source: The Railroad Gazette  1906-04-20: Vol 40 Iss 16 (1906-04-20), page image n12, archive.org sim_railway-age_1906-04-20_40_16 (https://archive.org/details/sim_railway-age_1906-04-20_40_16/page/n12); published in the United States before 1931, public domain

plates.caption: 'Big Pine Camp': a construction camp under the trees on Big Pine Key, from F. E. Spooner's report in The Railroad Gazette, 26 April 1907, p. 583. Spooner visited 'nearly every one of the 25 or more construction camps'.
plates.source: The Railroad Gazette  1907-04-26: Vol 42 Iss 17 (1907-04-26), page image n16, archive.org sim_railway-age_1907-04-26_42_17 (https://archive.org/details/sim_railway-age_1907-04-26_42_17/page/n16); published in the United States before 1931, public domain

plates.titel: The Moser Channel drawbridge during erection
plates.caption: 'Moser Channel Drawbridge During Erection': the swing span on its pier in open water, Railway Age Gazette, 10 May 1912, p. 1040. Steel girders on concrete piers carried the line over Knight's Key and Moser Channel; in October 1909 five girders were blown off their piers.
plates.source: Railway Age Gazette  1912-05-10: Vol 52 Iss 19 (1912-05-10), page image n11, archive.org sim_railway-age_1912-05-10_52_19 (https://archive.org/details/sim_railway-age_1912-05-10_52_19/page/n11); published in the United States before 1931, public domain

plates.titel: The first train at Key West, 22 January 1912
plates.caption: 'Arrival of first train at Key West, Fla., over sea, Florida East Coast R. R., Jan. 22, 1912': panoramic photograph, Library of Congress, cut from its mount. The company's booklet of the same year puts the line at 128.4 miles from Homestead.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Arrival of first train at Key West, Fla., over sea, Florida East Coast R. R., Jan. 22, (19)12 LCCN2007660721.tif (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Arrival_of_first_train_at_Key_West,_Fla.,_over_sea,_Florida_East_Coast_R._R.,_Jan._22,_(19)12_LCCN2007660721.tif)

plates.titel: Flagler and his party leave the first train
plates.caption: 'Mr. H. M. Flagler and party leaving first train to arrive at Key West': panoramic photograph, 22 January 1912, Library of Congress, cut from its mount. Flagler was eighty-two; he died the next year.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Mr. H. M. Flagler and party leaving first train to arrive at Key West, Fla. Oversea Florida East Coast R. R LCCN2007660733.tif (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mr._H._M._Flagler_and_party_leaving_first_train_to_arrive_at_Key_West,_Fla._Oversea_Florida_East_Coast_R._R_LCCN2007660733.tif)

plates.caption: Surface weather analysis for 2 September 1935, from the Monthly Weather Review, then published by the U.S. Weather Bureau: the storm as a closed low off the Florida Keys on the day it crossed them. A federal work.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Labor Day hurricane weather analysis (Enlarged), Sep 2, 1935.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Labor_Day_hurricane_weather_analysis_(Enlarged),_Sep_2,_1935.jpg)
